summary: Correct, minimal fix: always casting xa to int (not only in the float branch) prevents the out-of-bounds uint8 assignment that triggered the NumPy 1.24 deprecation warnings, and also fixes a latent correctness bug where over/under/bad indices silently overflowed integer-dtype inputs. errstate is appropriately narrowed to wrap the NaN→int cast.

issues.description: np.errstate(invalid="ignore") now wraps only the astype cast; the added comment explains the cast (unsigned ints + floats) but not why errstate is still needed there (suppressing 'invalid value encountered in cast' for NaN floats). A one-line note would aid future readers.

Float-branch comparisons (xa < 0) and np.clip are no longer inside errstate. In practice these don't emit invalid warnings (minimum/maximum and quiet ops; suite/CI with warnings-as-errors passes on NaN colormap inputs), so no real regression, but the scope reduction is worth a glance.
